사진 확대
Samsung Bioepis headquarters in Songdo, Incheon. [Samsung Bioepis]
Samsung Bioepis has entered the domestic approval process for its immuno-cancer drug "Kytruda" biosimilar, the world's largest-selling drug. Samsung Bioepis was the first to enter the application stage for product approval in Korea amid competition for the development of Keytruda biosimilars by global pharmaceutical and bio companies.
Samsung Bioepis announced on the 10th that it has applied for product approval for Keytruda biosimilar candidate SB27 (component name Pembrolizumab) to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.
Keytruda is an immuno-cancer drug developed by MSD in the United States and is the world's largest blockbuster drug with global sales of $31.7 billion (about 46 trillion won) last year. It is a mechanism that inhibits immune evasion of cancer cells by binding PD-1, an immune checkpoint receptor, and helps the human immune system attack cancer cells. It is used in various carcinomas and is leading the global anticancer drug market.
Samsung Bioepis applied for SB27's approval this time with a total of 16 diseases, including melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and head and neck cancer.
The Company confirmed the equivalence of the original drug and SB27 through large global clinical trials. Starting in 2024, phase 1 clinical trials were conducted on 163 patients in four global countries, and 555 patients from 14 global countries participated in phase 3 clinical trials.
As the market size of Keytruda is so large, competition for development by global biosimilar companies is also intensifying. Through this application, Samsung Bioepis was the first among the Keytruda biosimilars under development in Korea to enter the product approval process.
Shin Dong-hoon, vice president of Samsung Bioepis' clinical medicine division, said, "We will faithfully explain SB27's research and development results during this product approval review process and carry out related procedures without a hitch to provide immune anticancer drug treatment options to domestic patients as soon as possible."
Samsung Bioepis is currently selling a total of 11 biosimilars in Korea, including autoimmune diseases, tumor diseases, ophthalmic diseases, and rare disease treatments. Seven subsequent biosimilar pipelines are also being developed, including SB27.

Pharma Industry.url_match_title: Pharmaceutical quality controls fuel expansion of Karl Fischer titration reagent market through 2035 - chemicals.economictimes.indiatimes.com
Pharma Industry.content:
Water content determination becomes non-negotiable in regulated manufacturing
Pharmaceutical manufacturers cannot afford moisture errors. A single percentage-point variance in a drug formulation's water content can compromise shelf life, stability, or therapeutic efficacy. For lyophilised products, biologics, and injectable medications, the stakes are even higher. This relentless demand for precision is reshaping the market for
Karl Fischer titration
reagents, the analytical gold standard for moisture measurement in controlled environments.
According to
IndexBox
, a market research platform, the global Karl Fischer titration reagents market is projected to reach an index value of 170 by 2035 (using 2025 as a baseline of 100), corresponding to a 5.7 per cent compound annual growth rate over the decade. The expansion reflects structural demand from regulated industries where moisture control directly determines product viability and compliance.
Pharma quality assurance anchors demand
Pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies consume an estimated 35 per cent of global Karl Fischer reagents, according to
IndexBox
's analysis. The driver is simple: regulatory bodies including the
United States Pharmacopoeia
(USP), the
European Pharmacopoeia
(EP), and the
Japanese Pharmacopoeia
(JP) mandate precise moisture determination across the drug development and manufacturing pipeline. A formulation cannot proceed to production without validated moisture profiles. Shelf-life studies, stability testing, and batch release all hinge on these measurements.
The sector is undergoing a technological shift. Automated Karl Fischer titration systems, which integrate sample handling, moisture analysis, and data management in a single workflow, are replacing manual labour-intensive benchtop protocols. This shift drives consumption in two ways: laboratories purchasing new instruments require compatible reagents, and automated systems consume higher volumes of high-purity reagents than manual alternatives because they operate continuously and at standardised conditions.
Lyophilised formulations present a particularly acute need. Freeze-dried drugs, used in biologics and injectable medications, contain residual moisture measured in tenths of a per cent. Missing this precision is not an option. IndexBox notes that the expansion of biopharmaceutical manufacturing capacity, particularly in Asia-Pacific, will lock in demand for quality control reagents well into the 2030s.
Clinical diagnostics
racing ahead
The clinical diagnostics segment, though smaller at an estimated 25 per cent market share, is growing faster than pharmaceuticals. IndexBox projects annual growth of 6 to 8 per cent for this segment, outpacing the overall market rate. The driver is the decentralisation of laboratory testing. Point-of-care devices, satellite laboratories, and distributed testing networks require moisture analysis for reagent calibration, control materials, and quality assurance at the site of use, not at a centralised facility.
This shift reshapes product demand. Ready-to-use, single-dose ampoules of Karl Fischer reagent are gaining traction in clinical settings because they eliminate the contamination risk of multi-use bottles and reduce training overhead. A technician simply breaks open a sealed ampoule and loads it into the instrument. For diagnostics companies managing thousands of distributed testing points, this convenience translates into higher per-unit reagent costs but lower operational friction.
Roche Diagnostics
,
Siemens Healthineers
,
Abbott Laboratories
, and
Bio-Rad Laboratories
are among the major participants driving this shift, according to IndexBox.
Chemical manufacturing
and legacy processes
Chemical and petrochemical producers represent roughly 20 per cent of end-use demand. For these industries, Karl Fischer titration is not a quality mandate imposed by regulators but a practical requirement. Moisture content in solvents, polymers, and intermediates directly affects product performance and customer specifications. A solvent that absorbs too much water from the air becomes unusable. A polymer with residual moisture loses structural properties.
This segment operates differently from pharmaceuticals. Volume matters more than regulatory compliance. Standard-grade reagents at lower cost are preferred to high-purity, validated batches. However, the adoption of online and in-line titration systems, which perform moisture analysis at the point of production rather than in a laboratory, is driving incremental demand. The expansion of petrochemical capacity in the Middle East and Asia-Pacific will sustain this consumption through the forecast period.
Raw material volatility and supply-chain friction
Growth will not accelerate without constraint. IndexBox identifies several headwinds. Raw material costs for anhydrous methanol, iodine, and sulphur dioxide are volatile. These three ingredients are the core components of Karl Fischer reagents. Methanol, a key solvent, is produced from natural gas, making it exposed to energy-price fluctuations. Iodine supplies are concentrated in a handful of countries, including Chile and Japan, and geopolitical disruptions or production mishaps can drive spot prices sharply higher.
Regulatory compliance is another burden. Suppliers must invest heavily in validation, documentation, and quality assurance systems to meet USP, EP, and other pharmacopeial standards. For smaller manufacturers, these compliance costs can be prohibitive, driving consolidation toward larger, better-capitalised firms like
Merck KGaA
,
Thermo Fisher Scientific
,
Mettler-Toledo
,
Honeywell
, and
Avantor
.
Supply-chain disruptions in packaging and logistics add friction. Karl Fischer reagents are hazardous chemicals, classified as corrosive or flammable. Shipping restrictions, carrier capacity, and regulatory documentation can slow distribution, particularly to emerging markets where laboratory infrastructure is expanding fastest.
Alternative methods gaining ground slowly
Karl Fischer titration does not hold a monopoly on moisture determination. Loss on drying, a gravimetric method that heats a sample to constant weight, is simpler and cheaper but slower and less precise. Near-infrared spectroscopy can estimate moisture in some products non-destructively but requires calibration and is prone to matrix effects. For high-stakes applications, Karl Fischer remains the gold standard. But in cost-sensitive segments or where speed matters more than precision, these alternatives are chipping away at market share.
The market baseline and structural tailwinds
IndexBox's baseline scenario assumes steady, moderate growth driven by structural demand from regulated industries. The pharmaceutical sector's continued expansion, especially in emerging markets where drug manufacturing is being localised, will sustain demand for validated reagents and quality-control consumables. The replacement cycle of ageing titration instruments in established markets will drive consumables sales even in regions where installed capacity is mature. The recurring-revenue model of the
reagent market
, where laboratories must replenish supplies continuously, provides stability that capital equipment markets lack.
Clinical diagnostics' faster growth rate reflects the ongoing shift toward decentralised testing. As healthcare systems globally invest in point-of-care diagnostics and distributed laboratory networks, the footprint of Karl Fischer titration instruments will expand. Each new testing site is a potential customer for reagent supplies.
The pharmaceutical and biotech sector's dominance will persist, anchored by regulatory requirements that show no sign of relaxing. If anything, tighter quality standards, increased scrutiny of supply-chain resilience, and the growing complexity of biopharmaceutical manufacturing will intensify reliance on validated moisture-determination tools.
Winners and losers in the reagent supply ecosystem
Market consolidation will favour suppliers with global distribution, established compliance credentials, and the financial capacity to absorb raw material price swings. Smaller, regional manufacturers face margin pressure and the burden of maintaining multiple pharmacopeial certifications across different geographies. Partnerships between reagent suppliers and equipment manufacturers are likely to intensify, as customers prefer integrated solutions that guarantee compatibility and reduce qualification burden.
The shift toward ready-to-use formats presents a distinct opportunity. Suppliers that can manufacture sealed, sterile ampoules at scale and distribute them efficiently will capture share in clinical diagnostics. This format commands a price premium but reduces customer risk and operational complexity.
Forward outlook and market structure
The market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals than in prior years. Procurement decisions are becoming more disciplined, with laboratories evaluating total cost of ownership rather than unit price alone. Supply architecture is diversifying away from a handful of suppliers, particularly in Asia-Pacific where local manufacturing capacity is expanding. These structural shifts reduce the risk of supply shocks and create more stable, predictable growth trajectories.
By 2035, the market is expected to be larger, more geographically balanced, and more segmented by end-use application and product format.
Pharmaceutical quality control
will remain the anchor. Clinical diagnostics will be the growth engine. Chemical manufacturing will be steady but undynamic. Suppliers that can serve all three segments with tailored products and regional logistics will command competitive advantage.
The index of 170 by 2035 does not denote explosive growth. It reflects the maturity of the market and the steady, underlying demand from regulated industries. But for suppliers and their customers, this stability is valuable. In a world of volatile raw materials and fragmented supply chains, predictable demand for a critical quality-assurance tool is an asset worth cultivating.

Pharma Industry.content:
Pharmaceutical giant Bristol Myers Squibb plans to invest $2.3B to build a 600K SF manufacturing campus in Northeast Houston’s Generation Park,
the company announced Monday
.
Photo credit: Bristol Myers Squibb
A rendering of Bristol Myers Squibb's Houston campus
The Houston campus, expected to create nearly 500 skilled jobs, will be “modular and multi-modal,” designed with flexibility to grow and reconfigure to meet future pipelines and commercial needs.
BMS’ announcement comes nearly a year after pharmaceutical giant
Eli Lilly
confirmed it would
build a $6.5B synthetic medicine
active
pharmaceutical
product facility in Generation Park, a 4,300-acre master-planned district from
McCord Development
.
“
Bristol Myers Squibb
’s announcement is a tremendous win for Texas and the Houston region, further reinforcing our position as a premier destination for life sciences and advanced manufacturing,”
Greater Houston Partnership
CEO Steve Kean
said in a statement
, adding that the investment will strengthen Houston’s standing as a leading hub for life sciences innovation and investment.
BMS selected Texas and
Generation Park
following an extensive evaluation of competitive markets in the central and eastern U.S., the company said. BMS said the local life sciences workforce, incentives, proximity to utilities and transportation infrastructure, and a business climate conducive to long-term growth were factors in its selection of Houston.
“This highly competitive process validates the role our site plays as a vital life science asset both in Texas and nationally,” Generation Park Management District Executive Director Jennifer Mott said. “Our commitment to critical investments in infrastructure and a curated ecosystem continues to attract high-value industry clusters that drive long-term prosperity for the region.”
Eli Lilly chose Generation Park for its facility from a list of more than 300 proposals and applications.
McCord officials said
infrastructure, speed to market, and educational and workforce partnerships helped them land the investment.
BMS, a New Jersey-based biopharmaceutical company that researches, develops and creates medicines to treat serious diseases, said this announcement is part of its planned five-year, $40B investment across U.S. research and development, technology and domestic manufacturing.
The Houston campus’s multimodal design will allow BMS to manufacture several types of medicines, such as small molecules, biologics and antibody-drug conjugates.
“This investment reflects our confidence in America's continued leadership in biopharmaceutical innovation,” Bristol Myers Squibb CEO Christopher Boerner said. “As part of our $40 billion commitment to the United States, we're building the domestic manufacturing capabilities needed to deliver the next generation of medicines and support future scientific breakthroughs. Houston and the state of Texas offer the talent, infrastructure, and partnership needed to help bring that vision to life.”

Piston Pump Systems Market to Reach 170 Index by 2035 on UHPLC and SFC Adoption in Pharma R&D
Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global
Piston Pump Systems market
, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global piston pump systems market is entering a sustained expansion phase, with demand projected to rise at a compound annual growth rate of 5-7% from 2026 to 2035. This growth is underpinned by the accelerating adoption of ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography (UHPLC) and supercritical fluid chromatography (SFC) in pharmaceutical R&D, clinical diagnostics, and semiconductor process chemistry. Integrated systems remain the largest value segment, capturing an estimated 45-50% of global revenue, while consumables and replacement parts are gaining share as installed bases mature and aftermarket procurement intensifies. Supply-side constraints, including extended supplier qualification timelines and precision-component capacity limitations, continue to shape lead times and pricing structures across all major regions. The market is also witnessing a technology migration toward higher-pressure, lower-dead-volume pump architectures, with premium systems capable of 15,000-20,000 psi gaining preference in quality-control laboratories. Aftermarket service contracts and validated consumable programs are becoming standard procurement vehicles, with 50-60% of new integrated system sales now bundled with multi-year service commitments. Regional supply chain diversification is accelerating, as buyers in North America and Europe qualify second-source suppliers in Southeast Asia and Central Europe to reduce dependency on single regions for critical components.
The baseline scenario for the world piston pump systems market points to steady growth through 2035, with the market index rising from 100 in 2025 to approximately 170 by 2035, reflecting a CAGR of 5-7%. This outlook is supported by robust demand from pharmaceutical and biotech R&D, where UHPLC and SFC are becoming standard tools for method development and quality control. The semiconductor industry is another major growth pillar, as advanced chip manufacturing requires ultra-clean, high-pressure pumps for chemical delivery and wafer processing. Industrial automation and robotics are driving demand for precision fluid control in factory settings, while OEM integration favors compact, modular, and customizable pump systems. The aftermarket segment is expanding as the installed base of piston pump systems grows, with replacement parts and consumables contributing an increasing share of revenue. However, the market faces challenges from supply-side constraints, including long qualification cycles for precision-machined components and volatility in raw material prices for specialty alloys and ceramics. Regulatory fragmentation across regions adds compliance costs and lengthens time-to-market. Despite these headwinds, the overall trajectory remains positive, with innovation in pump design and materials enabling higher performance and reliability, thereby supporting adoption across diverse end-use sectors.
Demand Drivers and Constraints
Primary Demand Drivers
Rising adoption of UHPLC and SFC in pharmaceutical R&D and clinical diagnostics
Growing demand for ultra-clean high-pressure pumps in semiconductor manufacturing
Expansion of industrial automation and robotics requiring precision fluid control
Increasing aftermarket demand for consumables and replacement parts as installed base matures
Technology migration toward higher-pressure, lower-dead-volume pump architectures
Regional supply chain diversification and second-source qualification initiatives
Potential Growth Constraints
Extended supplier qualification cycles (6-12 months) for precision components
Volatility in raw material prices for specialty alloys, ceramics, and seals
Regulatory fragmentation across major markets increasing compliance costs
High initial investment for premium-grade pump systems limiting adoption in cost-sensitive regions
Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Pharmaceutical & Biotechnology (estimated share: 30%)
In the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sector, piston pump systems are essential for high-performance liquid chromatography, which is widely used in drug discovery, method development, and quality assurance. The shift toward more complex biologics and personalized medicines is driving the need for precise, reproducible fluid delivery at pressures up to 20,000 psi. Through 2035, the demand for these systems is expected to grow as regulatory agencies require more rigorous analytical testing, and as the industry moves toward continuous manufacturing processes. Key demand-side indicators include R&D spending by major pharma companies, the number of new drug approvals, and the expansion of contract research and manufacturing organizations. The trend toward miniaturization and higher throughput in analytical labs also supports the adoption of advanced piston pump systems with lower dead volumes and faster cycle times. Current trend: Increasing adoption of UHPLC and SFC for drug development and quality control.
Major trends:
Shift to UHPLC and SFC for faster, more efficient separations, Growing use of online monitoring and process analytical technology, Increased demand for biocompatible pump materials, and Expansion of contract research and manufacturing services.
Representative participants:
Agilent Technologies, Waters Corporation, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Shimadzu Corporation, and PerkinElmer.
Semiconductor & Electronics (estimated share: 25%)
The semiconductor industry relies on piston pump systems for precise delivery of chemicals, slurries, and solvents in processes such as photolithography, etching, and chemical mechanical planarization. As chip geometries shrink and wafer sizes increase, the need for ultra-clean, contamination-free pumps with high pressure and flow accuracy becomes critical. The market is driven by the expansion of advanced node manufacturing, the growth of 5G and AI applications, and the increasing complexity of semiconductor devices. Through 2035, demand is expected to accelerate as new fabs come online and as existing facilities upgrade to meet stricter purity and performance standards. Key indicators include capital expenditure by major chipmakers, fab utilization rates, and the adoption of advanced packaging technologies. The trend toward localized production and supply chain resilience also influences sourcing decisions, with manufacturers seeking reliable suppliers of precision pump components. Current trend: Rising demand for ultra-clean, high-pressure pumps for chemical delivery and wafer processing.
Major trends:
Adoption of ultra-high-purity materials and coatings, Integration of smart sensors and IoT for predictive maintenance, Shift toward modular and scalable pump designs, and Increased focus on reducing total cost of ownership.
Representative participants:
IDEX Corporation, Parker Hannifin, Entegris, Iwaki Co., Ltd, and Nikkiso Co., Ltd.
Industrial Automation & Robotics (estimated share: 20%)
Industrial automation and robotics are increasingly adopting piston pump systems for tasks that require precise fluid metering, lubrication, and cooling. The push toward Industry 4.0 and smart factories is driving the integration of pumps with sensors, controllers, and data analytics, enabling real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance. As manufacturers seek to improve efficiency and reduce downtime, the demand for reliable, high-performance pumps is rising. Through 2035, the market will benefit from the expansion of automated production lines, the growth of collaborative robots, and the need for energy-efficient fluid handling solutions. Key demand-side indicators include industrial robot shipments, factory automation spending, and the adoption of digital twins and predictive maintenance technologies. The trend toward modular and compact pump designs is also supporting integration into space-constrained robotic systems. Current trend: Growing use of precision fluid control in factory automation and robotic systems.
Major trends:
Integration of IoT and Industry 4.0 technologies, Development of energy-efficient and compact pump designs, Growing use of predictive maintenance and condition monitoring, and Expansion of collaborative robots and flexible automation.
Representative participants:
Bosch Rexroth, Eaton Corporation, Parker Hannifin, KNF Neuberger, and ProMinent GmbH.
OEM Integration & Maintenance (estimated share: 15%)
OEMs across various industries, including analytical instruments, medical devices, and industrial equipment, require piston pump systems that are tailored to their specific application needs. This segment is driven by the trend toward modular and customizable pump designs that can be easily integrated into larger systems. Additionally, the aftermarket for maintenance and replacement parts is growing as installed bases age and as end-users prioritize uptime and reliability. Through 2035, the demand for OEM integration is expected to rise with the proliferation of new analytical and diagnostic instruments, while the maintenance segment will benefit from the increasing complexity of pump systems and the need for specialized service expertise. Key indicators include OEM production volumes, the number of new instrument launches, and the adoption of service contracts and predictive maintenance programs. Current trend: Increasing demand for customized, modular pump systems and lifecycle support services.
Major trends:
Rise of modular and configurable pump platforms, Growth of service contracts and consumable bundling, Increasing use of digital twins for design and maintenance, and Expansion of aftermarket parts and refurbishment services.
Representative participants:
Agilent Technologies, Waters Corporation, IDEX Corporation, Parker Hannifin, and KNF Neuberger.
Environmental & Water Treatment (estimated share: 10%)
Piston pump systems are used in environmental applications such as water and wastewater treatment, chemical dosing, and environmental monitoring. The need for accurate and reliable fluid delivery in these applications is driven by stricter environmental regulations and the growing focus on sustainable water management. Through 2035, demand is expected to grow as municipalities and industries invest in upgrading water infrastructure and as the need for advanced treatment processes increases. Key demand-side indicators include public and private investment in water infrastructure, the adoption of advanced oxidation processes, and the expansion of environmental monitoring networks. The trend toward energy-efficient and low-maintenance pumps is also influencing purchasing decisions, with end-users seeking solutions that reduce operational costs and environmental impact. Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 40%)
Asia-Pacific dominates the market, driven by rapid industrialization, expanding semiconductor manufacturing, and growing pharmaceutical R&D in China, Japan, and South Korea. The region is also a major production hub for precision components, with supply chain diversification efforts attracting investments in Southeast Asia. Direction: Fastest growth.
North America (estimated share: 30%)
North America remains a key market, supported by strong pharmaceutical and biotech sectors, advanced semiconductor fabs, and a focus on reshoring critical manufacturing. The presence of major pump manufacturers and early adoption of UHPLC and SFC technologies sustain demand. Direction: Steady growth.
Europe (estimated share: 20%)
Europe's market is driven by stringent environmental regulations, a robust industrial automation base, and significant investment in pharmaceutical R&D. The region is also a hub for precision engineering, with Germany and Switzerland leading in pump innovation. Direction: Moderate growth.
Latin America (estimated share: 5%)
Latin America is an emerging market with growing demand from water treatment and mining industries. Economic volatility and limited local manufacturing are challenges, but increasing infrastructure investment and regulatory modernization are expected to support gradual growth. Direction: Emerging growth.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 5%)
The Middle East & Africa region shows slow but steady demand, primarily from oil and gas, water desalination, and emerging industrial sectors. Investment in infrastructure and diversification away from hydrocarbons is expected to create opportunities for pump suppliers. Direction: Slow growth.

Pharma Industry.url_match_title: US Pharma India Pvt. Ltd.: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing - Prime Insights Magazine
Pharma Industry.content:
US Pharma India Pvt. Ltd.
Did you know that the pharmaceutical industry touches nearly every stage of human life—from preventive healthcare and chronic disease management to life-saving treatments and advanced therapies?
Today, the global pharmaceutical sector stands among the most dynamic and competitive industries, driven by rapid technological advancements, evolving regulations, increasing healthcare demands, and the constant pursuit of innovation. Companies operating in this space must balance stringent quality standards, regulatory compliance, affordability, and patient safety while continuously adapting to changing market expectations. In such a highly regulated and innovation-driven environment, only organizations committed to excellence, reliability, and continuous improvement can build lasting trust and sustainable growth.
Among the companies making a meaningful impact in this sector is
US Pharma India Pvt. Ltd.
, a pharmaceutical formulations manufacturing company dedicated to delivering high-quality, safe, and affordable healthcare solutions. Guided by the visionary leadership of
Mr. Tapan Sanghvi, Managing Director
, the company has established itself as a trusted name in pharmaceutical manufacturing. With a strong entrepreneurial mindset and an unwavering commitment to quality, compliance, and innovation, Mr. Sanghvi has played a pivotal role in shaping the company’s growth journey. His leadership philosophy emphasizes patient-centricity, ethical business practices, operational excellence, and long-term value creation. Through strategic investments in technology, research, and talent development, he has successfully transformed
US Pharma India Pvt. Ltd.
into a future-ready organization that continues to earn the trust of customers and healthcare stakeholders.
Founded with a vision to build a reliable and quality-focused pharmaceutical enterprise,
US Pharma India Pvt. Ltd.
specializes in formulations manufacturing, innovative drug delivery mechanisms, and healthcare solutions that address diverse therapeutic needs. The company operates through robust Quality Management Systems, GMP-compliant processes, advanced manufacturing technologies, automation, and digitalization to ensure product consistency, safety, and regulatory compliance. Its commitment to research, continuous improvement, sustainability, and affordable healthcare has enabled the organization to strengthen its presence across domestic and international markets while delivering meaningful healthcare outcomes.
In the spotlight is
Mr. Tapan Sanghvi, Managing Director,
in an exclusive interview for our prestigious
“Excellence in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing & Innovation”
edition. Explore his inspiring entrepreneurial journey, leadership philosophy, and valuable insights on building a world-class pharmaceutical organization. Stay tuned to discover his remarkable tale of success and learn the lessons that continue to drive excellence, innovation, and sustainable growth in the healthcare industry.
Prime Insights: Can you introduce your company and share its core mission in pharmaceutical manufacturing and innovation?
US Pharma India Pvt. Ltd.
is a formulations manufacturing company committed to delivering high-quality, safe, and affordable healthcare products while adhering to stringent regulatory and quality standards. Our mission is to improve lives through reliable manufacturing practices, innovation, operational excellence, and a patient-centric approach.
Prime Insights: What inspired the establishment of your organization, and how has your journey evolved over the years?
The company was established with the vision of building a trustworthy organization that combines quality, compliance, and innovation. Over the years, we have expanded our manufacturing capabilities, strengthened quality systems, invested in employee development, and enhanced our operational efficiency to meet evolving market and customer requirements.
Prime Insights: What are the key pharmaceutical products, therapies, or solutions that define your portfolio?
Our portfolio includes
[APIs /Finished Dosage Forms / Contract Manufacturing Services]
serving diverse therapeutic and industrial requirements. We continuously focus on delivering products that meet stringent quality and customer specifications. We have niche drug delivery mechanism for multiple products which helps patients.
Prime Insights: How do you ensure the highest standards of quality, safety, and compliance in your manufacturing processes?
At US Pharma India Pvt Ltd., we ensure the highest standards of quality, safety, and compliance through a comprehensive and robust Quality Management System embedded across all our operations. Our approach is built on a strong culture of quality, continuous improvement, and adherence to national and international regulatory requirements.
Our key practices include:
Robust Quality Management Systems (QMS)
Strict adherence to Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)
Implementation of Good Documentation Practices (GDP)
Risk-based quality management approaches
Regular internal audits and effective Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) systems
Continuous employee training and competency development programs
Stringent process monitoring, qualification, and validation activities
Implementation of best practices aligned with international standards and evolving global regulatory expectations
Supported by a skilled workforce, modern manufacturing capabilities, and a culture of accountability, we continuously strengthen our systems, processes, and controls to ensure consistent product quality, patient safety, data integrity, and regulatory compliance. This enables us to reliably deliver high-quality pharmaceutical products while maintaining customer trust and operational excellence.
Prime Insights: What role does innovation play in your product development and operational strategy?
We focus on adopting advanced technologies, digitalization, automation, and data-driven approaches to optimize manufacturing processes, strengthen quality systems, and enhance operational efficiency. Innovation plays a pivotal role in our Research & Development (R&D) efforts, supporting the development of novel drug delivery mechanisms, continuous product improvements, process optimization, and efficient, sustainable manufacturing solutions.
In our operations, we emphasize continuous improvement, technology absorption, risk-based decision-making, and employee capability development to drive productivity and maintain high standards of quality and compliance.
Prime Insights: Can you highlight a major milestone or achievement that reflects your company’s excellence in the pharmaceutical sector?
Over the years, we have successfully implemented robust Quality Management Systems, enhanced operational efficiencies through the adoption of advanced technologies, and expanded our capabilities to meet the evolving requirements of both domestic and international markets.
We have also developed novel drug delivery mechanisms for several products, helping improve patient convenience, treatment effectiveness, and overall healthcare outcomes.
A core pillar of US Pharma India Pvt. Ltd. is our commitment to ensuring that patients have access to high-quality medicines at affordable prices. This patient-centric approach has enabled our products to gain wide acceptance and trust among healthcare professionals and consumers alike.
These achievements reflect our unwavering focus on innovation, quality, accessibility, and sustainable growth, reinforcing our position as a reliable and responsible pharmaceutical company.
Prime Insights: How do you leverage advanced technologies, automation, and digitalization to enhance manufacturing efficiency?
We leverage advanced technologies, automation, and digitalization to build a smart, efficient, and quality-driven manufacturing ecosystem. Our ISO-certified manufacturing facility operates in accordance with internationally recognized quality management standards, ensuring consistent product quality, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement.
Our facilities utilize data-driven systems for real-time process monitoring, production planning, inventory management, and quality control.
Automation helps streamline repetitive tasks, optimize resource utilization, reduce downtime, and ensure strict adherence to regulatory and quality standards. We also embrace digital transformation through integrated enterprise systems that strengthen cross-functional collaboration, improve supply chain visibility, and enhance overall operational agility.
Through continuous investments in technology, process innovation, and ISO-compliant systems, we create a sustainable and future-ready manufacturing environment that delivers safe, effective, reliable, and high-quality pharmaceutical products while consistently meeting customer and industry expectations.
Prime Insights: What measures do you take to ensure regulatory compliance with national and international standards?
Adherence to applicable GMP guidelines
Regular internal audits
Regulatory updates and gap assessments
CAPA implementation and monitoring
Employee compliance training
Comprehensive documentation and record management
Prime Insights: How does your organization contribute to improving healthcare accessibility and patient outcomes?
Through continuous investment in research and development, advanced manufacturing technologies as well as we ensure the consistent availability of reliable healthcare solutions that support better treatment outcomes and enhance patients’ quality of life.
We work closely with healthcare professionals, distributors, and strategic partners to strengthen supply chain efficiency and ensure timely access to medicines across various markets. Our patient-centric approach focuses on identifying unmet medical needs, improving treatment accessibility, and supporting healthcare systems with innovative and effective solutions.
By combining scientific expertise, operational excellence, and a strong commitment to continuous improvement, we contribute to building a healthier future and creating a positive impact on communities worldwide.
Prime Insights: Can you share a success story where your products or innovations made a significant impact on the healthcare industry?
As a long-term player in the healthcare sector, our measure of success is largely defined by customer loyalty, reflected through consistent repeat orders and long-standing business relationships. We are proud to share that many of our customers have remained associated with us throughout our journey, which is a testament to the trust they place in our quality, reliability, and commitment to excellence. Their continued partnership motivates us to consistently deliver high-quality products and create long-term value for all stakeholders.
Prime Insights: How do you foster a culture of research, innovation, and continuous improvement within your organization?
We encourage collaboration, knowledge sharing, and a proactive approach to problem-solving across all levels of the organization. Our dedicated Research & Development (R&D) team continuously focuses on developing new formulations, enhancing existing products, and exploring novel drug delivery mechanisms while adopting advanced technologies to address evolving healthcare needs. We also promote a culture of continuous improvement by empowering employees to contribute innovative ideas, optimize processes, and drive operational excellence across the organization.
We invest in employee training, digitization, and process optimization to enhance operational efficiency, product quality, and regulatory compliance. Cross-functional teams regularly evaluate opportunities for improvement, implement best practices, and leverage automation to strengthen manufacturing capabilities.
In addition, our strong quality management systems support a culture of excellence, ensuring that innovation is aligned with the highest standards of quality, safety, and patient well-being. Through continuous learning and a commitment to innovation, we strive to deliver sustainable value to healthcare professionals, patients, and stakeholders worldwide.
Prime Insights: What initiatives have you undertaken in sustainability, environmental responsibility, and ethical manufacturing?
Environmental Management
Ethical Manufacturing Practices
ISO-Certified Manufacturing Facility
Technology and Process Optimization
Employee Awareness and Engagement
Sustainable Growth
Energy and Resource Conservation
Water Recovery and Conservation
Prime Insights: How do you address challenges such as supply chain disruptions, changing regulations, and evolving market demands?
We adopt a proactive, agile, and risk-based approach to effectively address industry challenges and ensure business continuity while maintaining the highest standards of quality, compliance, and customer satisfaction.
Our approach includes:
Strengthening Supply Chain Resilience:
We maintain a diversified supplier network, establish strategic partnerships,
Regulatory Compliance and Adaptability:
We continuously monitor evolving regulatory requirements across domestic and international markets and ensure timely implementation through robust quality management systems, regular audits, and ongoing employee training.
Market Intelligence and Customer Focus:
We actively analyse market trends, customer needs, and healthcare demands to quickly adapt our product portfolio and business strategies.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Our teams across manufacturing, quality assurance, regulatory affairs, procurement, and commercial operations work collaboratively to ensure quick decision-making and seamless execution.
By combining operational excellence, innovation, regulatory vigilance, and customer-centricity, we remain resilient, responsive, and well-positioned to navigate a rapidly evolving pharmaceutical landscape while continuing to deliver safe, effective, and high-quality healthcare solutions.
Prime Insights: What are your future plans for expanding your product portfolio, manufacturing capabilities, and global presence?
Expanded manufacturing capabilities by adding multiple new facilities to strengthen and diversify the product portfolio.
Introducing new products and advanced technologies to enhance innovation and operational efficiency.
Expanding domestic and international market presence through product registrations and strategic distribution partnerships in new countries.
Prime Insights: What advice would you give to emerging pharmaceutical companies striving for excellence in manufacturing and innovation?
My advice to emerging pharmaceutical companies would be to build a strong foundation centered on quality,
patient safety
, innovation, and long-term sustainability rather than focusing solely on rapid growth.
Prioritize Quality
Invest in Research & Development
Adopt Advanced Technologies
Build Strong Regulatory and Compliance Capabilities
Develop a Resilient Supply Chain
Invest in People and Organizational Culture
Commit to Sustainability and Ethical Manufacturing

Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. reported past first-quarter 2026 results showing sales of ¥116,160 million versus ¥127,536 million a year earlier, while net income rose to ¥24,151 million and earnings per share also increased.
Separately, Phylo, Inc. announced a collaboration with Ono to deploy its Biomni Lab agentic AI platform, potentially sharpening Ono’s research productivity and helping explain how profitability improved despite lower sales.
With stronger earnings on lower sales and a new AI collaboration shaping operations, we now examine how this combination affects Ono’s investment narrative.

What Is Ono Pharmaceutical's Investment Narrative?
To own Ono Pharmaceutical, you have to be comfortable with a story built around disciplined profitability, a broad collaboration network and a pipeline that needs to offset revenue pressure. The latest quarter crystallizes that tension: sales slipped, yet net income and EPS improved, suggesting tighter cost control or a richer mix of higher-margin products. That matters for the near term, because key catalysts are now less about sheer top line growth and more about how efficiently Ono converts its R&D and partnerships into earnings. The new Phylo AI collaboration fits directly into this, potentially reinforcing productivity gains that helped lift profits despite softer revenue, although the financial impact is unlikely to be immediate. At the same time, guidance still points to revenue and earnings declines, so execution risk around the pipeline and partnerships remains front and center.
However, one risk that could catch some investors off guard sits beneath those improving margins.
Ono Pharmaceutical's shares have been on the rise but are still potentially undervalued by 34%.

Pharma Industry.url_match_title: Bristol Myers Squibb Invests $2.3B in New Houston Pharma Facility - Greater Houston Partnership
Pharma Industry.content:
Pharmaceutical giant Bristol Myers Squibb will invest
$2.3 billion
to build a 600,000-square-foot manufacturing facility at Generation Park in northeast Houston. The project is expected to create nearly 500 jobs and reflects the growing momentum behind Houston’s life sciences sector.
“As part of our $40 billion commitment to the United States, we’re building the domestic manufacturing capabilities needed to deliver the next generation of medicines and support future scientific breakthroughs,” said Bristol Myers Squibb Board Chair and CEO Christopher Boerner, Ph.D. “Houston and the state of Texas offer the talent, infrastructure, and partnership needed to help bring that vision to life.”
According to a press release, BMS said the manufacturing facility will “be a modular, multi-modal campus,” allowing it to scale beyond its initial configuration to meet pipeline and commercial demands. BMS will manufacture multiple types of medicines, such as small molecules, biologics and antibody-drug conjugates. Construction of the facility is expected to begin in 2027 with operations slated to start in 2030.
The Partnership, alongside regional partners, played a key role in attracting the New Jersey-based biopharmaceutical company to the region.
“Bristol Myers Squibb’s announcement is a tremendous win for Texas and the Houston region, further reinforcing our position as a premier destination for life sciences and advanced manufacturing,” said Greater Houston Partnership President and CEO Steve Kean.
Learn more about
Houston’s life sciences and biotech ecosystem
by connecting with the Partnership’s Global Life Sciences Sr. Director
Verena
Kallhoff
.
Growing Investment in Houston’s Life Sciences Ecosystem
Last year, Eli Lilly and Company announced a $6.5 billion pharmaceutical manufacturing facility at Generation Park. Together, the projects reflect years of coordinated regional work to build the workforce, infrastructure and business environment needed to attract large-scale, for-profit life sciences investment. McCord Development, the developer of Generation Park, has played a central role in translating that regional strategy into a site prepared for major life sciences and biomanufacturing projects.
RELATED:
Houston Wins Texas’ First Major Pharma Plant With $6.5B Investment
“We are grateful for this strong endorsement of Generation Park as a home for advanced life science manufacturing,” said Ryan McCord, CEO and President of McCord Development. “With beautiful parks, resilient infrastructure, higher education workforce development, and certainty of execution, Generation Park attracts jobs and supports the industry producing next-generation therapies.”
Why Houston
Houston offers a strong mix of research institutions, workforce training, available real estate and a business-friendly environment that supports companies at every stage of growth.
The region is home to six medical schools, three Tier One research universities and specialized training programs through San Jacinto College’s NIBRT-licensed Center for Biotechnology, Lone Star College and Texas A&M’s National Center for Therapeutics Manufacturing. Houston has also attracted a growing roster of life sciences companies, from homegrown firms like Neurogene and CellReady to relocations including BioNova Scientific and Cellipont.

life sciences companies are choosing Houston
.

Pharma Industry.url_match_title: US bill could subject China-to-US pharma licensing deals to national security controls - AllSci
Pharma Industry.content:
Senators Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) and Pete Ricketts (R-NE)
introduced
the Biotech Investment National Security Act (BINSA) on August 6, 2026, a bipartisan bill that would bring pharmaceutical licensing deals, joint ventures, and equity investments involving Chinese entities under the federal outbound investment screening framework established by the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security (COINS) Act. The legislation amends Title VIII of the Defense Production Act of 1950 to classify pharmaceutical development, biologics manufacturing, and clinical research capabilities as "prohibited" or "notifiable" technologies when transferred to covered foreign persons — principally entities subject to the direction or control of the People's Republic of China (PRC). Companion legislation was introduced in the House
in June 2026
by Representatives John Moolenaar (MI-02) and Debbie Dingell (MI-06).
What it covers
BINSA
would formally add biotechnology — defined to encompass pharmaceutical products, biological products, therapeutic compounds, drug discovery platforms, clinical research and development (R&D) capabilities, biologics manufacturing, and related intellectual property and know-how — to the list of sectors subject to federal outbound investment screening. Qualifying transactions could become prohibited or subject to Treasury notification requirements, depending on the implementing regulations, with the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the Department of Defense (DoD), and the Director of National Intelligence (DNI) set to define the precise parameters of the biotechnology sector.
The bill excludes agricultural biotechnology, industrial fermentation unrelated to pharmaceutical production, and basic academic research with no direct therapeutic application. Separately, the Secretary of Defense would be required to submit a report within 60 days of enactment assessing whether US capital flows into Chinese biotechnology — including through licensing transactions — negatively affect national security and military readiness.
Why it matters
The bill's congressional findings cite approximately USD 136 billion in cross-border out-licensing transactions between US and European pharmaceutical companies and Chinese biotechnology firms in 2025 alone — a figure the legislation characterizes as an accelerating transfer of pharmaceutical innovation capacity to entities under PRC direction. However, it should be noted that much of the recent dealmaking boom has involved Chinese biotechs licensing internally developed drug candidates to US and European companies — meaning IP rights flow westward while capital flows to China.

Pharma Industry.url_match_title: China’s biotech surge paves way for home-grown pharma powerhouse - Qatar Tribune
Pharma Industry.content:
+ A
A -
Qatar tribune
Agencies
Thanks to an efficiency edge that transcends simple cost advantages, China is set to see the emergence of a home-grown drug giant capable of competing with global players in a decade, analysts say.
“For the past three decades, there was only one global research and development ecosystem, which was the US,” said Fu Wei, founder and CEO of CBC Group, a healthcare-dedicated asset management firm founded in Shanghai and now based in Singapore.
“Over the past decade, a parallel ecosystem – China – has emerged. We are not only more cost-efficient, but also faster [in drug innovation], and its edge is irreversible,” he said during a panel discussion at the Global Health Summit in Hong Kong on Friday.
“Ten years from now, we will definitely see a Chinese Big Pharma emerging in its home market.” However, Fu said that building a globally competitive pharmaceutical powerhouse with Chinese roots will be a long-term process.
“The biopharma industry – unlike other industries – requires years of regulatory approvals, deep product pipelines with hundreds of new drugs, and next-generation technologies before companies can achieve a meaningful market impact,” Fu said.
Once this vision materialised, it would mark a significant change from the current landscape, where China’s innovative drug market remains dominated by foreign multinationals, Fu said, pointing to AstraZeneca as an example. The Swedish-British company’s innovative drug sales in China surpass those of local leader Hengrui Pharma, he noted.
Once known primarily for low-margin generic manufacturing, China’s pharmaceutical sector has undergone a wave of innovation.
This transformation has been reflected in a surge of out-licensing deals for innovative drugs, with their total value reaching a record $110 billion in the first half of this year, state broadcaster CCTVreported.
Currently, China accounts for roughly 30 per cent of the world’s novel drugs under development, ranking second globally, CCTV said. Iris Wang, founding partner and chief investment officer at Hong Kong-based TruMed Investment, noted that China’s biotech sector is expanding at a pace that has caught the market off guard.
“It was only over the past two to three years, as the West saw these out-licensing deals, that they finally realised how fast China’s biotech sector had grown,” Wang said.
“They undervalued our pace of innovation.” Wang noted that China’s biotech boom is rooted in systemic efficiency – built on infrastructure, policy support, and a deep talent pool – making it difficult to replicate elsewhere in the near term.
With biopharmaceuticals designated an emerging pillar industry alongside integrated circuits, aerospace and others in its latest five-year plan, Beijing has pledged to deepen its support for the sector.
In a blueprint for China’s healthcare development over the next five years released by the State Council in July, authorities have committed to providing full-chain support for drug innovation, while pledging faster regulatory approvals for critical therapies and improved clinical evaluation frameworks to boost hospital adoption.
Wang said she anticipated sustained momentum for Chinese drug innovators, noting that China’s systemic efficiency is well positioned to drive breakthroughs in frontier domains such as AI-driven drug development.
“Some mistakenly assume that because the US leads in AI, it will naturally dominate biotech in the future,” Wang said. “But in drug discovery, AI models alone are not enough. What truly matters is whether that computational power can be converted into data validated in the lab, and ultimately, validated in clinical trials.
“Pioneering in AI drug discovery right now requires systemic leadership across AI, biology, and lab operations,” she said. “China is building a whole new paradigm here, giving the country advantages to take the lead in the next phase of drug innovation.”

Pharma Industry.content:
Camille MacMillin/STAT
By
Allison DeAngelis
Aug. 10, 2026
Biotech Startups and Venture Capital Reporter
Allison DeAngelis
[email protected]
Allison covers what hot startups are getting up to, and who’s financing them. She is also co-host of the weekly biotech podcast, “
The Readout Loud
.” You can reach Allison on Signal at AllisonDeAngelis.01.
In cancer treatment, the pitch has been simple: What if, instead of blasting radiation across patients’ bodies, crop-dusting not only malignant cells but also neighboring healthy tissues, we could shoot chemical weapons directly at only the noxious tumors?
That has been the central promise of radiopharmaceuticals, which have grabbed the drug industry’s attention and created a
shining new field of drug development
. But, as more and more of these therapies move into clinical trials, developers are finding it’s not so clear-cut.
Advertisement
The isotopes that make up radiopharmaceuticals are just as virulent as the beam radiation patients have begrudgingly tolerated for decades. They are designed to be far more targeted. But while they’re hurtling to biological bull’s-eyes, some are inadvertently zapping patients’ kidneys, liver, or bone marrow along the way.

Pharma Industry.content:
Major Regulatory Milestone Positions Company to Initiate Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase 2 Study of Patented First-in-Class Neuroprotective Therapy Targeting Demyelination
Lucid-MS Advances Novel Disease-Modifying Approach Targeting Multi-Billion Dollar Progressive MS Market with Significant Unmet Medical Need Worldwide
TORONTO, Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Quantum BioPharma Ltd. (NASDAQ: QNTM) (CSE: QNTM) (FRA: 0K91) ("
Quantum BioPharma
”), a transformative biopharmaceutical company dedicated to building a portfolio of innovative assets and biotech solutions for challenging neurological, metabolic, and alcohol misuse disorders, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Company’s Investigational New Drug (IND) application for Lucid-MS (Lucid-21-302), enabling Quantum BioPharma to immediately advance its patented, first-in-class multiple sclerosis program into Phase 2 clinical development. This will be the first time in history patients with MS consume the unique Lucid-MS new chemical entity molecule with a goal of reversing some or all of their loss of bodily control or mobility.
This strategic milestone clears a pivotal regulatory pathway, enabling Quantum BioPharma to begin its planned Phase 2 clinical trial of Lucid-MS in individuals with progressive multiple sclerosis (MS). The Company is working with a leading global clinical research organization with significant experience in neurodegenerative studies, to support implementation of the planned disease-modifying Phase 2 study. Trial start-up activities, including site selection, are already underway, and the Company expects to initiate patient enrollment and drug administration as quickly as possible.
Addressing a Substantial Unmet Medical Need

Progressive forms of MS-including primary progressive MS (PPMS) and secondary progressive MS (SPMS)-represent an area of substantial unmet medical need worldwide, with limited therapeutic options currently available. According to market research, the Primary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (PPMS) Treatment Market is projected to expand from USD $1.16 billion in 2025 to USD $1.31 billion by 2026, reflecting a CAGR of 13.7% (The Business Research Company, 2026). The overall global MS therapeutics market is anticipated to reach approximately USD $38.62 billion by 2030, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.93% (Grand View Research, 2026). Despite the availability of disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), a substantial proportion of patients with progressive MS remain untreated or continue to experience disability progression, highlighting the critical need for innovative treatments that not only modulate the immune response but also promote remyelination and neuroprotection.
Lucid-MS is a patented, new chemical entity investigational drug candidate designed to provide neuroprotection through the inhibition of demyelination, a key contributor to disability progression in multiple sclerosis. Unlike most existing therapies that focus primarily on modulating the immune system, Lucid-MS represents a differentiated approach targeting the underlying neurodegeneration-a novel mechanism with the potential to address the root cause of disease advancement in progressive MS.
Advertisement
CEO Statement: A Transformative Moment for Quantum BioPharma
"The IND submitted was approximately 15,000 pages long and the approval from the FDA for Lucid-MS permits Quantum BioPharma to proceed with the Phase 2 clinical trial. This Phase 2 trial marks an important strategic milestone for Quantum BioPharma and advances our unique Lucid-MS program into the next stage of development," said Zeeshan Saeed, Founder, Chief Executive Officer, and Executive Co-Chairman of the Board of Quantum BioPharma.
Mr. Saeed added, "Lucid-MS represents a unique patented first-in-class, disease-modifying therapeutic opportunity in multiple sclerosis by targeting demyelination, particularly in progressive forms of the disease where unmet medical needs remain today. Our strong balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation provide a runway for meaningful clinical data generation, and we look forward to delivering results that could transform outcomes for millions of patients worldwide who currently have no effective treatment alternatives. This is not just a regulatory checkpoint-it is a breakthrough moment to try to demonstrate, possibly for the first time, that neuroprotection is achievable."
Scientific Leadership Highlights Trial Design and Translational Relevance
Advertisement
"This strategic milestone supports advancement of a first-in-class program evaluating a novel neuroprotective strategy in progressive multiple sclerosis," said Andrzej Chruscinski, M.D., Ph.D., Vice-President, Scientific and Clinical Affairs at Quantum BioPharma. "The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial is intended to evaluate efficacy using clinical and radiological measures relevant to disability progression and disease biology, while also assessing safety and tolerability. This rigorous trial design meets the highest FDA standards and reflects our commitment to generating meaningful clinical data that can support a clear path toward regulatory submission and potential future approval."
Dr. Chruscinski continued, "Progressive MS has long been an area of frustration for neurologists and patients alike, given the paucity of effective interventions. Lucid-MS offers a differentiated approach-it does not suppress the immune system but instead works to preserve myelin integrity and neuronal function. We believe this novel mechanism could fundamentally change how clinicians approach progressive MS, and we are excited to move into this pivotal phase of development."
First-in-Class Therapeutic Innovation
Lucid-MS is designed to provide neuroprotection through the inhibition of demyelination-a key driver of disease progression in MS. This innovative mechanism represents a differentiated therapeutic approach in the global MS market, where most existing therapies focus primarily on modulating the immune response rather than addressing the underlying neurodegeneration. By targeting protein arginine deiminase 2 (PAD2), a key enzyme implicated in myelin degradation, Lucid-MS has demonstrated in preclinical models the ability to prevent and reverse myelin breakdown-offering the potential for a truly disease-modifying therapy in an indication with limited options.
Advertisement
The Phase 2 clinical trial will evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of Lucid-MS in people with MS. In prior Phase 1 clinical trials, Lucid-MS demonstrated a favorable safety profile and was well-tolerated in healthy participants, providing a strong foundation for continued development. The successful completion of Phase 1 supports advancement into this next pivotal study, which is designed to generate meaningful clinical data across both clinical and radiological endpoints.
Strategic Partnership and Trial Execution
Quantum BioPharma is partnering with a globally recognized clinical research organization, to support the implementation of the Lucid-MS Phase 2 clinical trial. This strategic collaboration is designed to ensure efficient patient enrollment, rigorous data collection, and regulatory compliance throughout the study. Site selection is currently underway, with patient enrollment and drug administration to begin as quickly as possible.
The Company's decision to engage a global leading CRO with experience in neurodegenerative diseases, reflects its commitment to operational excellence and rapid advancement of its clinical programs. This partnership approach mirrors industry best practices, as demonstrated by other leading biotech companies advancing pivotal programs in neurodegenerative diseases.
Advertisement
Financial Position and Runway
Quantum BioPharma maintains a strong balance sheet to support its clinical development programs. The Company reported cash, digital assets and liquid investments totaling over USD $10 million as of March 31, 2026.
Market Context: Neurology Sector Momentum
The announcement comes amid a period of renewed investor confidence in neurology-focused biotech stocks. The BioWorld Neurological Diseases Index (BNDI) finished 2025 up 6.33%, recovering from a midyear slump (BioWorld, 2026). This rebound indicates a favorable investment environment for companies advancing disease-modifying therapies in challenging neurological indications. In April 2026, several NASDAQ-listed biotechnology companies specializing in neurology and MS have experienced notable spikes in trading volume, driven by significant corporate developments and clinical advancements. Biogen (BIIB), Neurocrine Biosciences (NBIX), and Lexicon Pharmaceuticals (LXRX) have all attracted investor interest through positive clinical data and regulatory progress.
Advertisement
Lucid-MS: A Differentiated Candidate in a Multi-Billion Dollar Market
Progressive MS represents a multi-billion-dollar market opportunity with limited competition. While established players such as Biogen and Sanofi focus primarily on immunomodulatory approaches, Lucid-MS is positioned as a first-in-class, non-immunomodulatory agent with the potential to address the underlying cause of disease progression - demyelination. This novel mechanism could enable Quantum BioPharma to capture significant market share in an indication where patients and physicians are seeking new solutions.
The Company's lead molecule, Lucid-MS, is a patented, new chemical entity that has demonstrated excellent efficacy in various preclinical animal models over many years, accelerating functional recovery of mouse models of MS, preserving myelin, and reducing axonal degradation. Lucid-MS does not suppress the immune system unlike most current therapies for MS today, offering potential oral administration with an easy dosing regimen-a significant advantage for patient compliance and quality of life.
About Quantum BioPharma Ltd.
Advertisement
Quantum BioPharma Ltd. is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to building a portfolio of innovative assets and biotech solutions for the treatment of challenging neurodegenerative and metabolic disorders and alcohol misuse disorders with drug candidates in different stages of development. Through its wholly owned subsidiary, Lucid Psycheceuticals Inc. ("Lucid”), Quantum is focused on the research and development of its lead compound, Lucid-MS. Lucid-MS is a patented new chemical entity shown to prevent and reverse myelin degradation, the underlying mechanism of multiple sclerosis, in preclinical models. Quantum invented UNBUZZD™ and spun out its OTC version to a company, Unbuzzd Wellness Inc. ("Unbuzzd”) (formerly, Celly Nutrition Corp.), led by industry veterans. Quantum retains ownership of 19.84% (as of March 31, 2026) of Unbuzzd at www.unbuzzd.com. The agreement with Unbuzzd also includes royalty payments of 7% of sales from unbuzzd™ until payments to Quantum total $250 million. Once $250 million is reached, the royalty drops to 3% in perpetuity. Quantum retains 100% of the rights to develop similar products or alternative formulations specifically for pharmaceutical and medical uses.

Medical devices are not pharma products, companies say while opposing Draft Bill
Agencies
Synopsis
India’s medical device industry and healthcare groups have opposed the draft Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics Bill, 2026, arguing that treating medical devices like pharmaceuticals and imposing criminal penalties for regulatory lapses could hurt manufacturing, investment and innovation.
By
Teena Thacker
,
ET Bureau
Aug 11, 2026, 12:09:00 AM IST
Follow us
New Delhi: Medical device industry, patient safety groups and
healthcare providers
have opposed the draft Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics Bill, 2026, saying it treats medical devices like medicines and will hurt manufacturing and innovation, people in the know told ET.
ADVERTISEMENT
Several associations representing manufacturers, traders, healthcare providers and patient groups have written to the Union health minister urging a rethink of the draft, warning that it will hurt investment, discourage manufacturing and set back India's ambition of becoming a global medical device hub.
In its pushback against the draft bill, the medical device industry has cited that medical devices are engineering products not pharmaceuticals and cannot be regulated as drugs.
ET was first to report that the government was preparing to replace the 86-year-old law governing India's pharmaceuticals regulations.
The draft bill is currently under inter-ministerial consultation.
The associations in their August 8 letter have submitted that the draft bill does not provide the regulatory foundation required for India's medical devices sector to grow, innovate, and compete globally.
ADVERTISEMENT
"The draft continues to treat medical devices as an adjunct to pharmaceuticals, despite clear scientific, engineering, and regulatory distinctions between the two categories," the letter said. ET has seen the copy of letter.
The industry has expressed their concern over the draft as it continues to use drug-centric language with terms like "adulterated", "spurious", and "misbranded," and applies pharma-style criminalisation to engineering deviations.
ADVERTISEMENT
ADVERTISEMENT
"Globally, medical devices are regulated through risk-based conformity assessments, quality management systems, post-market surveillance, and recalls, not imprisonment," it said.
The draft bill imposes imprisonment of 1-7 years for labelling errors, documentation lapses, licensing issues, PMS reporting mistakes, engineering defects, even when no harm occurs.
"This is not practiced in EU MDR,
US FDA
, Japan PMDA, UK MHRA, or Australia TGA, where administrative enforcement is the norm," it said.

Economic Times WhatsApp channel

How big is the Fragment-Based Drug Discovery Market in 2026?
USD 1.9 billion in 2026 and USD 5.6 billion by 2036 at an 11.4% CAGR.
Demand for fragment-based drug discovery is projected to expand at 11.4% CAGR between 2026 and 2036, raising valuation from USD 1.9 billion to USD 5.6 billion. Growth is being supported by the rising scale of fragment-screening programs, which require specialized capabilities for hit identification and lead optimization. Diamond Light Source reported in September 2025 that a dengue polymerase screening campaign evaluated 1,108 fragments and identified 60 structural hits, highlighting the large screening volumes needed to generate viable development candidates. Drug developers rely on service providers that can integrate structural biology and medicinal chemistry within a single workflow.
The United Kingdom continues to strengthen its position in fragment-based drug discovery through investments in high-throughput structural screening infrastructure and translational research partnerships. In February 2025, Cancer Research Horizons and Diamond Light Source established a partnership to build a world-leading fragment-based drug discovery program, expanding the use of XChem fragment screening and improving experimental throughput and analysis capabilities. The collaboration reflects growing demand for scalable fragment-screening platforms capable of supporting both academic and commercial drug discovery projects.
Fragment Based Drug Discovery Market Value Analysis
Key Takeaways
Discovery teams use compact fragments to address difficult pockets that conventional libraries cannot reach efficiently.
Fragment screening platforms are projected to account for 39.0% by product in 2026 due to controlled starting-point quality.
Nuclear magnetic resonance screening is estimated to hold 31.0% by technology in 2026 owing to flexible solution-phase confirmation.
Oncology is expected to capture 37.0% by application in 2026 because mutation-specific programs require precise structural guidance.
Weak affinity restricts adoption as unstable proteins and assay interference produce misleading signals without orthogonal confirmation.
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc., Evotec SE, WuXi AppTec Co., Ltd., Domainex Ltd., Sygnature Discovery Ltd., Astex Pharmaceuticals, Sprint Bioscience AB and Cresset serve distinct fragment-based discovery roles.
Analyst Perspective
"Fragment screening earns commercial value when weak hits survive orthogonal confirmation and receive practical chemistry plans. Project sponsors should compare protein readiness with structural evidence before assigning difficult targets to outsourced FBDD programs."
-
Anurag Sharma
, Principal Consultant, Future Market Insights
How is the Fragment-Based Drug Discovery Market segmented?
The fragment-based drug discovery industry is segmented by product, technology, application, end user, workflow and region.
Product coverage includes screening platforms and fragment libraries alongside software and specialist services for commercial discovery programs. Technology includes nuclear magnetic resonance screening, X-ray crystallography, surface plasmon resonance and computational screening while applications cover oncology, neurological disorders, infectious diseases and metabolic or rare diseases. End users include pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology companies, contract research organizations and academic or research institutes. Workflow analysis follows hit identification, lead optimization and preclinical candidate selection across connected evidence and chemistry decisions.
What makes oncology central to the application category?
Fragment Based Drug Discovery Market Analysis By Application
Oncology programs frequently pursue mutation-defined pockets and protein interfaces that resist conventional screening across heterogeneous tumor biology. Fragment-derived compounds need target-engagement evidence and
molecular diagnostics
context to secure broader preclinical investment across commercial programs.
Based on application, oncology is projected to account for 37.0% share in 2026 due to mutation-specific programs that require compact starting molecules and structural guidance.
Astex presented April 2026 MYC inhibitor results that applied fragment-based discovery to direct small-molecule inhibition of a difficult cancer regulator. Structural evidence helps oncology teams judge selectivity ahead of committing commercial resources to longer optimization campaigns across validated target programs.
What supports fragment screening platforms within the product category?
Fragment screening platforms organize library selection and assay controls around a defined route toward orthogonal confirmation across varied target classes. Consistent
protein expression
prevents weak signals from consuming medicinal chemistry capacity during expensive fragment expansion decisions that govern project continuity.
By product, fragment screening platforms are estimated to hold 39.0% share in 2026 owing to their control over starting-point quality and downstream chemistry efficiency.
Protein readiness determines whether screening signals survive transfer into structural and
high-content screening
assays across partner workflows. Sprint Bioscience reported in June 2025 that its SciLifeLab partnership added advanced protein-quality analysis to fragment-based development.
How does nuclear magnetic resonance screening shape technology selection?
Nuclear magnetic resonance screening detects weak interactions in solution with ligand-observed and protein-observed measurements across varied targets. The method preserves binding evidence in solution before structural teams commit limited crystallography capacity.
In 2026, nuclear magnetic resonance screening is expected to lead technology demand with 31.0% share because complementary observation modes support primary screening and confirmation.
Surface plasmon resonance
measures kinetics across prioritized fragments as X-ray crystallography resolves binding geometry for structural design. Integrated
bioinformatics tools
preserve experimental records so teams can compare evidence across successive chemistry cycles.
What role do pharmaceutical companies play within the end-user category?
Pharmaceutical companies coordinate target biology with structural analysis and medicinal chemistry under governed portfolio decisions and multiyear budgets. Specialist
clinical research organizations
add capacity without separating confirmation from later optimization and candidate-selection decisions.
Pharmaceutical companies are set to lead the end-user category with 43.0% share in 2026 due to coordinated funding and accountable ownership across long discovery programs.
Biotechnology companies and academic institutes use modular partners as internal capacity remains narrow or project timing requires specialist methods. Integrated providers reduce handoff risk by preserving assay records and chemistry rationale across organizational boundaries and portfolio governance.
What are the drivers, restraints and opportunities in the Fragment-Based Drug Discovery Market?
Difficult-target programs support fragment-led discovery as weak affinity raises confirmation costs and automated structural workflows expand usable hit capacity.
Driver: Commercial validation directs compact libraries toward pockets that larger screening compounds cannot address efficiently.
Restraint: Weak fragment affinity requires stable proteins and sensitive assays before medicinal chemistry teams commit further resources.
Opportunity: Automated crystallography and covalent libraries increase actionable starting points as computational ranking directs limited experimental capacity.
Fragment-derived assets gain commercial credibility through transactions that reward early discovery quality. Sprint Bioscience completed the TREX1 sale to Gilead in November 2025 with USD 14 million upfront and potential payments reaching USD 400 million. The agreement rewards clear target biology and transferable chemistry plans.
Protein instability or assay interference can generate false signals across repeated experiments. Qualified
analytical testing services
establish reproducibility across assay transfers and protect chemistry capacity. Written stop criteria prevent recurring synthesis work from absorbing limited specialist budgets.
Covalent fragments stabilize weak target engagement and reveal binding sites that reversible libraries miss. Automated crystallography and
AI-enabled design
rank those hits before wider synthesis campaigns. Providers capture revenue by connecting validated binding with rapid analogue production and medicinal chemistry.
